blocks.text: Greek colonists from Megara founded Byzantion on the Bosphorus around 660 BCE; legend names their leader Byzas. They chose the site well: a hilly peninsula between the Sea of Marmara and the deep harbour of the Golden Horn, commanding the strait between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean.

In 324 the Roman emperor Constantine chose the town for a new capital, and on 11 May 330 it was dedicated as Constantinople, the city of Constantine. For more than a thousand years it was the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire, which historians call Byzantine. Its great church, Hagia Sophia (*Ayasofya*), was built in 532–537, and its land walls, begun under Theodosius II in the early 5th century, held off besiegers for centuries.

In 1204 the armies of the Fourth Crusade sacked the city, and the Byzantines only recovered it, weakened, in 1261. On 29 May 1453, after a siege of 55 days, the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II took it, and it became the Ottoman capital. Ottoman documents called it *Kostantiniyye*, while people also used the name *İstanbul*, first recorded in the 10th century and most likely from the Greek words “eis tin polin”, to the city.

The Ottomans rebuilt and enlarged it: Topkapı Palace from the 15th century, the Süleymaniye Mosque by the architect Sinan in 1550–1557, covered bazaars, fountains and whole neighbourhoods of wooden houses. In October 1923 the new Republic made Ankara its capital, and on 28 March 1930 a postal law made *İstanbul* the city's only official name.

Today Istanbul is Turkey's largest city, with about 15.8 million people at the end of 2025, spread over both banks of the Bosphorus: part of the city is in Europe, part in Asia. Its historic peninsula and the land walls, the Historic Areas of Istanbul, have been on UNESCO's World Heritage List since 1985.

blocks.title: Two sides
blocks.text: Istanbulites speak of the European side, *Avrupa Yakası*, and the Asian side, *Anadolu Yakası*. Ferries (*vapurlar*) cross between them all day, and many people commute by boat.
Here is the city in the Turkish of this unit:

blocks.tr: İstanbul büyük bir şehir. İstanbul'da güzel müzeler var. Ayasofya Sultanahmet'te. Boğaz'da vapurlar var.
blocks.en: Istanbul is a big city. There are beautiful museums in Istanbul. Hagia Sophia is in Sultanahmet. There are ferries on the Bosphorus.

questions.q: Which city replaced Istanbul as the capital in 1923?
Where does the name *İstanbul* most likely come from?
questions.explain: It is first recorded in the 10th century, long before the Ottoman conquest, and most likely comes from “eis tin polin”.
